papers.title: Certification Time for Weak-Force-Mediated Entanglement between Levitated Particles
papers.authors: Yao-Tong Chen; Salambô Dago; Oriol Romero-Isart; Andreu Riera-Campeny
papers.problem: Experiments with levitated nanoparticles aim to show that a weak force, and eventually gravity, entangles the motion of two particles. Producing the entangled state is only half the task: it has to be told apart from separable states using a finite number of noisy measurements, taken one run at a time. How many measurements, and how much laboratory time, does certification need, and which protocol reaches the weakest forces?
papers.result:
For a two-mode Gaussian state with smallest partially transposed symplectic eigenvalue \(	ilde
u_-<1\), certification at \(z\) standard deviations needs about \(N_\star=(z\alpha/(1-	ilde
u_-))^2\) measurements. With isotropic readout noise \(\xi\), \(\alpha\ge	ilde
u_-+\xi\), with equality for symmetric thermal two-mode squeezed states, while local squeezing leaves the entanglement unchanged and makes \(\alpha\) arbitrarily large. In release–recapture, at a fixed ratio of diffusion to coupling, the entanglement stays finite as the force weakens but \(N_\star\) grows as \(1/g\) and the total time as \(g^{-3/2}\). Release–recapture certifies entanglement at couplings orders of magnitude weaker than continuous monitoring, and the release time that certifies fastest is longer than the one that entangles most.
techniques: Delta-method error bars for a covariance witness
Weak-coupling limit at a fixed noise-to-coupling ratio

papers.title: Qubit-environment entanglement in pure dephasing dynamics for mixed initial states
papers.authors: Małgorzata Strzałka; Nico Peters; Laura Ares; Jan Sperling; Katarzyna Roszak
papers.problem: When a qubit only dephases, the joint qubit–environment state for a pure initial qubit is separable exactly when the environment ends up in the same state whichever pointer state the qubit is in, \(\hat R_{00}(t)=\hat R_{11}(t)\). This test made it possible to tell decoherence by entanglement from decoherence by classical correlations, and even to detect the difference on the qubit alone. Real qubits are already partly mixed. Does the test survive, and does entanglement then evolve as it does for pure qubits?
papers.result: If \(\hat R_{00}(t)=\hat R_{11}(t)\), the joint state stays separable, and zero-discord, for any initial qubit coherence. Otherwise, the family of minors that gave the pure-state criterion becomes only a witness: a negative minor proves entanglement, but nonnegative minors prove nothing. A Schur complement reduces the exact partial-transpose test to a matrix \(\hat D\) of the environment’s dimension, whose diagonal entries are those minors. Mixed qubits show behaviour impossible for pure ones: a separable initial period followed by sudden birth of entanglement, death and rebirth, and no entanglement at all during an entangling evolution when the qubit is strongly mixed. In a model of an NV-centre spin with up to five nuclear spins, the minors miss entanglement, sometimes for the whole evolution.
techniques: Schur-complement reduction of a partial-transpose test
Common eigenbasis as a certificate of classical dephasing

papers.title: Meet-in-the-Middle Compilation of the [CNOT] Class with Fibonacci Anyons
papers.problem: Two qubits encoded in six Fibonacci anyons live in a five-dimensional fusion space, one dimension more than two qubits need. The only exchange that entangles the qubits, \(\sigma_3\), is also the only one that couples them to the fifth, noncomputational state, so every entangling braid leaks. How small can the leakage of a braid equivalent to CNOT up to single-qubit gates be at a given length, and is exhaustive search better than random sampling?
papers.result: A GPU meet-in-the-middle search over all \(5^{21}\) positive words finds at length 21 a braid with leakage \(\ell=3.95\times10^{-3}\) and distance \(7.8\times10^{-9}\) to the CNOT class, less leakage than the best previously sampled braid of length 39. Restricting to \(\{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\}\), to words starting and ending with \(\sigma_3\), to palindromes and to Garside normal forms extends exhaustive search to length 72; at length 69 it finds \(\ell=8.8\times10^{-11}\) with distance \(4.3\times10^{-10}\). The paper proves that leakage lies in \(\mathbb Z[\varphi]\) and that any nonzero leakage satisfies \(\ell\ge1/(1+C^{2L})\) with \(C\approx2.89\), and that for long random words the leakage distribution tends to \(\ell^{d-1}\).
techniques: Galois-conjugate lower bound on an algebraic quantity
Haar limit of one matrix element and the cost of sampling

papers.title: Quantum State Preparation for Complex-Valued Amplitudes
papers.problem: Quantum algorithms often compute numbers into binary registers with reversible arithmetic, but then need those numbers as amplitudes. For a complex \(z=x+iy\), the usual route encodes \(x\) and \(y\) separately and adds them with a linear combination of unitaries, which fixes the normalisation by the ranges of \(x\) and \(y\). How can \(z/\alpha\) be loaded coherently, for inputs in superposition, with a normalisation set by \(|z|\) itself?
papers.result: The procedure computes the magnitude \(r'\) and argument \(\phi'\) of \(z\) reversibly with CORDIC, which uses only shifts and additions. It then encodes \(r'/\alpha\) with an exact binary-to-amplitude routine, applies one phase gate per bit of \(\phi'\) to obtain \(e^{i\phi'}\), and uncomputes the arithmetic. The cost is \(O(n^2)\) Toffoli and \(T\) gates and \(O(n)\) ancillas, with error \(|r'e^{i\phi'}-z|=O(2^{-(n-l)})\) for \(n\)-bit inputs with \(l\) integer bits. A reversible in-place multiplication by \(1+2^{-2j}\), exactly invertible despite rounding, lets each CORDIC step run without storing an extra copy of a coordinate.
techniques: CORDIC: rotation by shifts and additions
Exact inversion of a rounded in-place product

papers.title: Prepare-and-measure quantum key distribution from a bound on information leakage
papers.authors: Abhishek Mishra; Michele Masini; Maria Balanzó-Juandó; Armin Tavakoli; Stefano Pironio
papers.problem: Every key distribution protocol has to limit what escapes the users’ laboratories. In a prepare-and-measure protocol this cannot be strict, since the source must send out a signal that depends on Alice’s private input. The minimal assumption is therefore a bound on how much the emitted systems, intended signal and side channels together, reveal about the input. Can that single number replace a model of the source’s states, dimension and energy, with nothing assumed about Bob’s measurement device?
papers.result: Yes, against collective attacks. The leakage bound states that the optimal number of correctly guessed inputs, out of \(n\) sent once each, is at most \(G\), with \(G=2\) meaning one bit. Statistics reproducible by a classical message within the same bound certify no key. This rules out all two-state protocols such as B92, and all matched-basis protocols such as BB84 and the six-state protocol. Tilting Bob’s measurements restores security: four qubit protocols certify one secret bit per key round in the ideal case, through a self-test on a virtual entanglement-based twin. With noise, the best tolerates visibility 0.838 (8.1% bit error rate) and the loss thresholds are \(\eta\ge0.764\), about 1.2 dB. Numerically, the rates match the device-independent rates of the entanglement-based twins.
techniques: Leakage as an operator inequality, and a virtual entanglement-based protocol
Copy-the-message attacks on classical models with bounded information

papers.title: Matrix Samplers and Quantum-Proof Extractors: Their Correspondence and Almost-Optimal Constructions
papers.problem: To estimate the average of a bounded \(D\times D\) matrix-valued function in operator norm, \(O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(2D/\delta))\) independent samples suffice, but each costs \(m\) fresh random bits. Matrix samplers try to keep nearly that sample count while using only \(m+O(\log(D/\delta))\) random bits. Classically, Zuckerman showed that averaging samplers and randomness extractors are the same objects. What kind of extractor is a matrix sampler, and can the correspondence give better constructions?
papers.result: A matrix sampler for \(D\times D\) matrices is the same thing as a seeded extractor whose output stays uniform against an adversary holding about \(\log(2D)\) qubits of side information, up to factor-two losses in the error. The paper then builds an explicit strong quantum-proof extractor with seed \((1+\alpha)\log a+(2+\alpha)\log(1/\eta)+O_\alpha(1)\) and output \(n-O_\alpha(a+\log(1/\eta))\) for sources of conditional min-entropy \(n-a\). Through the correspondence, this gives explicit strong matrix samplers with \(m+O_\alpha(\log(D/\delta))\) random bits and \(O_\alpha(\varepsilon^{-2-\alpha}\log^{1+\alpha}(D/\delta))\) samples, replacing a polynomial dependence on \(D\) in earlier work by a logarithmic one. It also gives quantum-proof extractors with seed \(O(\log(n/\eta))\) and output \(\Omega(n)\) for every constant entropy rate, where earlier constructions needed rate above one half.
techniques: Hermitian dilation turns a matrix deviation into a quantum distinguisher
Shortening a seed with 2ℓ-wise independent candidate seeds

papers.title: Experimental evidence for quantum Brownian motion in electron-metal decoherence
papers.authors: Wayne Cheng-Wei Huang; Zilin Chen; Herman Batelaan
papers.problem: Twenty years ago Anglin, Paz and Zurek proposed that an electron passing close to a metal loses coherence through quantum Brownian motion: its image charge dissipates energy in the metal, and by the fluctuation–dissipation theorem the same process randomizes the electron’s phase. Interferometer experiments near silicon found decoherence two orders of magnitude below the prediction, and those near gold were at the edge of detectability. Can electron–metal decoherence be measured and compared quantitatively with the theory?
papers.result: Yes, using a diffractometer instead of an interferometer. Diffracted 1.67 keV electrons enter a gold-plated microchannel at milliradian grazing incidence and bounce off the wall at sub-nanometre distance, which raises the interaction strength \(\Delta t/y^3\) to about \(10^7\) ps/μm³. All diffraction orders broaden equally and fringe visibility falls to 30–60%. The measured decoherence rate peaks at 182 μm⁻² at a tilt of 4.6 mrad, close to the classical-trajectory prediction of 216 μm⁻², and a standing-wave model reproduces the turnover at small tilt with a fitted gold resistivity of \(37\pm5\) nΩ m.
techniques: Integrating a local decoherence rate along a trajectory
Intra-beam coherence as a short-baseline decoherence detector

papers.title: Classical Verification of Quantum Computation Beyond the Polynomial Hierarchy
papers.problem: Can a classical polynomial-time verifier be convinced of the outcome of a quantum computation by the efficient quantum computer that ran it, with no cryptographic assumption? This is open for all of BQP, and every quantum problem known to have such a proof system lies in AM or was excluded only from MA relative to an oracle. Does efficient classical verification force a problem into the polynomial hierarchy?
papers.result: Not by any relativizing argument. Relative to a classical oracle, a variant of recursive Fourier sampling is decided exactly in quantum polynomial time, lies outside the polynomial hierarchy, and has a public-coin interactive proof with a classical verifier, an efficient quantum honest prover, perfect completeness and soundness error \(1/4\) against unbounded provers, using at most \(\log n/4\) messages. The message count can be made to grow as slowly as any unbounded computable function, and for a suitable oracle it is optimal up to a constant factor.
techniques: Recursive spot-checks with a height-independent soundness invariant
Switching under correlated projections via a rank bound

papers.title: Correlation-sensitive magic-state distillation from spin-squeezed neutral atoms
papers.authors: Ximo Wang; Ruyue Guo; Xinbo Li; Min Feng; Haozhe Wang; Zhenqi Bai; Yichi Zhang
papers.problem: Magic-state distillation is analysed for independent noisy inputs, with a fidelity threshold above which each round improves the resource. Neutral-atom factories prepare many resource blocks in parallel under shared interactions and control fields, which correlates their errors. Can such correlations defeat distillation even when every input is above threshold, and which measurable quantity decides?
papers.result: Yes. For the five-to-one Bravyi–Kitaev protocol with independent local Clifford twirls, the accepted output depends on the joint input only through sums \(A_k\) of \(k\)-body correlators along the target axis: \(p_{\rm acc}=(3+A_4)/48\) and \(t_{\rm out}=(A_3-2A_5)/(3+A_4)\). Distillation improves on the mean input exactly when \(G=A_3-2A_5-\bar t(3+A_4)>0\). Inputs with identical one- and two-qubit reduced states can have opposite gains, and in finite-range Ising simulations of a 25-atom source, interblock correlations reverse the gain while the product of the same local states gains.
techniques: Stabilizer expansion of a code projection on correlated inputs
Symmetry selection under code projection

papers.title: Measurement incompatibility and noiseless quantum codes
papers.problem: A quantum channel can destroy the incompatibility of measurements but never create it. Which channels preserve the incompatibility of every finite family of measurements? Chitambar and Zhang conjectured that, when the input is larger than the output, such a channel must carry a noiseless copy of its output space, and Uola and coauthors asked whether every dimension has a measurement family that is incompatible on the full space but compatible on every proper subspace.
papers.result: Both questions are settled. A channel from dimension \(D\) to \(d\) preserves all incompatibility if and only if an isometry \(W\) encodes every output state noiselessly, \(\mathcal N(W\rho W^\dagger)=\rho\). One explicit family of \(d^2\) binary measurements is a complete test: its compatibility threshold is \(s=1\), and any channel that keeps that threshold has such a code. The same family is incompatible on \(\mathbb C^d\) and compatible on every proper subspace, for every \(d\ge2\). If the threshold shifts by a small \(\delta\), an approximate encoding has diamond-norm error at most \(2c^2\delta^2\).
techniques: Dual-frame expansion of a dilation defect
Rigid parents of rank-one measurements

papers.title: Network nonlocality with tripartite entangled sources
papers.problem: Network nonlocality has mostly been studied with sources that emit pairs of particles. A three-qubit source has two distinct notions of nonlocality: the Mermin inequality excludes fully local models, and the Svetlichny inequality certifies genuine tripartite nonlocality. When independent sources emit three-qubit states and central nodes measure without any input, how is a network violation related to these two single-source tests?
papers.result: It depends on the wiring. In the closed network, where two input-free central nodes each hold one particle from every source, Bell-state measurements give a two-copy value at least the normalized Svetlichny value, \(\mathcal N_{\rm c}\ge\mathcal S/4\); every entangled generalized GHZ state, and even some biseparable states, violate the network inequality. In the open network, with one central node, the value is at most the normalized Mermin value, \(\mathcal N_{\rm o}\le\mathcal M/2\). With \(n\) sources, the largest violation of these two-correlator inequalities is \(\sqrt2\) (closed) or \(2\) (open) for even \(n\), but only \(2^{1/2-1/(2n)}\) or \(2^{1-1/(2n)}\) for odd \(n\).
techniques: Two perpendicular directions from one end node
Anticommutation bound for input-free central nodes

papers.title: Many-body entanglement quantification in arbitrary states through a few partial-transpose moments
papers.problem: Logarithmic negativity quantifies entanglement in mixed states, but computing it needs the full spectrum of the partial transpose and hence tomography. Moments of the partial transpose can be measured with randomized measurements or swap circuits. Given a few such moments, what is the largest amount of negativity they certify?
papers.result: Treating the normalized squared eigenvalues of the partial transpose as a probability measure turns the question into a truncated Hausdorff moment problem, solved exactly by Gauss or Gauss–Radau quadrature. The moments \(p_2,\dots,p_K\) give the best possible lower bound \(\mathcal E_K\). The bounds increase strictly until they become exact at \(K=4s\), where \(s\) is the number of distinct eigenvalue magnitudes, and converge for every state. For \(K=4\) the method reproduces the known bound \(\tfrac12\ln(p_2^3/p_4)\) and shows it is optimal.
techniques: Hermite interpolation certificate for moment problems
Saturation by counting spectral levels

papers.title: Bargmann-invariant witness of the graviton commutator
papers.problem: Experiments proposed to show that gravity is quantum look for gravitationally induced entanglement or decoherence, but Newtonian entangling phases can be mimicked by assigning a classical field to each branch, and decoherence can be mimicked by classical noise. Is there an interference observable that no branchwise-definite classical gravitational field can reproduce?
papers.result: Yes. For matter coupled linearly to linearized gravity, each branch coherence factorizes exactly into a conservative phase, the characteristic functional of the graviton state, and a phase from the field commutator. For two interferometers, the phase \(\mathfrak B\) of a four-cycle Bargmann invariant cancels everything except the commutator: it is independent of the graviton state and of all Newtonian interactions, and it vanishes for every branchwise-definite classical model. It is bounded by which-path decoherence, \(\mathfrak B^2\le16\,\Gamma_X\Gamma_Y\).
techniques: A cycle of coherences that cancels everything classical
Bounding a commutator signal by decoherence

papers.title: Self-Correcting 3D Surface Code with Growing Local Dimension
papers.problem: A self-correcting quantum memory keeps information for a time growing exponentially in a power of its size under local thermal dynamics, with no active correction. The 4D toric code achieves this, but in three dimensions a no-go theorem for fixed local dimension and the string-like logical operator of the 3D surface code stand in the way. Does allowing the local dimension \(q\) to grow with system size help?
papers.result: Yes. Changing only the Pauli powers of the 3D surface code along one axis, so that its string-like logical operator carries powers \(1,2,4,\dots\) modulo \(q\), gives a translation-invariant code in which, with odd \(q\ge cL^3\) and below a critical temperature, both error sectors have memory time at least \(e^{\Omega(N^{1/3})}\) under single-qudit Metropolis dynamics. Numerics suggest \(\log t_{\rm mem}\sim\min\{q,N^{1/3}\}\), so much smaller \(q\) may suffice.
techniques: Weighted chain complexes: change powers, keep supports
Energy against entropy, with a Lee-weight Boltzmann sum

papers.title: Distillable entanglement is continuous
papers.problem: Distillable entanglement, the best rate at which copies of a state can be turned into Bell pairs by local operations and classical communication, is defined operationally and has no single-letter formula. It was known to be lower semicontinuous and continuous on the interior of distillable states, but not continuous in general. Is it continuous everywhere, with an explicit bound?
papers.result: Yes. For states within trace distance \(\varepsilon<1/16\), \[|E_D(\rho)-E_D(\sigma)|\le4\sqrt\varepsilon\log d+4h(\sqrt\varepsilon),\] with \(d\) the smaller local dimension. The same bound holds for entanglement cost. The proof builds an explicit LOCC protocol that converts copies of \(\sigma\) into copies of \(\rho\) using a number of ebits per copy that vanishes as the states approach each other.
techniques: Continuity by a cheap conversion protocol
Locating rare outcomes with Grover search instead of measuring every copy

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced metrology with classical shadows
papers.problem: Reaching the best precision in quantum metrology usually requires measuring a specific, often complicated observable tailored to the probe and encoding. Can one instead measure every qubit in random Pauli bases, as in classical shadows, and still estimate a parameter well, and how much entanglement advantage survives?
papers.result: Yes, with a quantified cost. Combining all Pauli moments up to weight \(K\) from one randomized data set by generalized least squares gives variance \(1/(n\mathcal I)\), where the shadow information \(\mathcal I\) has a closed form. Separable probes reach at most \(\mathcal I=N/3\), so exceeding it witnesses entanglement, and no probe exceeds \(2N^2/(N+2)<2N\). Entanglement therefore gives a constant-factor gain, at most 6, not Heisenberg scaling: about 15% for twisted probes of 12 qubits.
techniques: Generalized least squares over correlated shadow moments
Separable benchmark for witnessing useful entanglement

papers.title: Exact Identification of Quantum Correlations in the Minimal Bell Scenario
papers.authors: Liang-Liang Sun; Jie Wang; Sixia Yu
papers.problem: In the simplest Bell experiment, two parties with two binary measurements each, the extreme points of the quantum set are known, but deciding whether a given list of eight statistics is quantum still requires searching over mixtures of many of them or climbing a semidefinite hierarchy that converges only in the limit. Is there an exact, finite test?
papers.result: Yes. A behaviour is quantum if and only if it is a mixture of a single behaviour produced by projective measurements on a pure two-qubit state and a local (classical) behaviour. The key step is a proof that every Bell functional with a strict quantum advantage has exactly one quantum maximizer. Membership then reduces to a system of trigonometric equations in five angles, and every quantum behaviour can be realized in dimension \(6\times6\).
techniques: A same-marginal local model that dominates every correlator
Eliminating mixture weights to test membership with five equations in five angles

papers.title: Ancilla-free optimal quantum adder
papers.authors: Junhong Nie; Jialiang Tang; Xiaoming Sun; Wei Zi
papers.problem: Quantum addition sits inside factoring, discrete logarithms and many oracles. Ripple-carry adders need no extra qubits but have linear depth; carry-lookahead adders reach logarithmic depth only with extra workspace. Can an exact \(n\)-bit adder have \(O(n)\) gates and \(O(\log n)\) depth with no ancillary qubits at all?
papers.result: Yes. Using only X, CNOT and Toffoli gates with all-to-all connectivity, the paper builds an exact ancilla-free adder with \(O(n)\) gates and \(O(\log n)\) depth, which is optimal for both. A simpler recursive version achieves \(O(n\log\log n)\) gates at the same depth. The construction borrows existing control and data wires as dirty workspace and always restores them.
techniques: Echoes: apply a map using dirty borrowed bits and restore them
Reducing addition to two controlled ladders

papers.title: Finite Nonsignalling Resources Suffice to Simulate Entangled Qubits
papers.authors: Ziao Tang; Xin Wang; Ge Bai
papers.problem: One PR box (a binary-input nonsignalling resource) plus shared randomness reproduces all projective-measurement statistics of a maximally entangled qubit pair. Some partially entangled states cannot be simulated with one PR box, and every known exact protocol for them uses a box with real-valued inputs. Is a continuous input alphabet necessary, as Gisin asked?
papers.result: No. For every pure state \(\cos\theta|00\rangle+\sin\theta|11\rangle\), shared randomness and at most \(K(\theta)=4\lceil\sqrt2\pi\cot^2\theta\rceil^2\le128\cot^4\theta\) PR boxes, used in parallel, reproduce all local projective statistics exactly, without communication or postselection. The budget does not depend on the measurement settings. The construction extends to every mixed two-qubit state and to all binary-outcome POVMs.
techniques: Exact sampling from an input-dependent density using a fixed shared list
A random-access index box from parallel PR boxes

papers.title: Certain Quantum States Already Require Quantum Time Evolution
papers.problem: Bell tests check quantum theory without assuming a model, but only its static structure. Could the dynamics be tested the same way? In phase-space theories where states are quasi-probability distributions and evolution is given by a generalized bracket, does the presence of certain states in the theory force the bracket to be the quantum (Moyal) one?
papers.result: Yes. Requiring that position and momentum marginals stay nonnegative under anharmonic evolution ties states to dynamics. If a particular superposition of the lowest three oscillator states is admissible, the bracket must be the Moyal bracket to all orders in \(\hbar^2\). If only the first excited oscillator state is admissible, the leading correction must equal the quantum value \(a_1=-1/24\). The ground state alone allows any \(a_1\) between the classical value 0 and \(-1/24\).
techniques: Positivity of marginals under evolution as a consistency test between states and dynamics
Zeros of a marginal as a short-time probe of higher-order terms

papers.title: Elementary proofs of quantum lower bounds for element distinctness and k-sum
papers.problem: Element distinctness needs \(\Theta(n^{2/3})\) quantum queries, but the known lower-bound proofs use the polynomial method, negative-weight adversaries or compressed oracles. The \(k\)-sum bound \(\Omega(n^{k/(k+1)})\) needs the negative-weight adversary. Can these bounds be proved with basic linear algebra?
papers.result: Yes, in under two pages each. Refining the hybrid argument of Bennett, Bernstein, Brassard and Vazirani, the proof tracks second-order differences of algorithm states under changes to two input positions. This gives \(E\|\psi_T(y)-\psi_T(x)\|^2=O(T/n+T^3/n^2)\) between a distinct input and one with a planted collision, hence \(T=\Omega(n^{2/3})\). With \(k\)th-order differences the same scheme gives \(\Omega(n^{k/(k+1)})\) for \(k\)-sum over groups with \(|G|\ge n^k\).
techniques: Hybrid argument with a sensitivity budget
Higher-order differences driven only by lower-order ones

papers.title: Entangled logical qubits on a superconducting quantum processor
papers.authors: Robin Harper; Xanda C. Kolesnikow; Campbell K. McLauchlan; Georgia M. Nixon; Stephen D. Bartlett; Benjamin J. Brown
papers.problem: On large superconducting chips, two effects not handled by standard surface-code circuits limit logical performance: leakage out of the qubit subspace and a fraction of underperforming qubits and couplers. Can a 120-qubit IBM processor with fast reset support logical memories, entangling operations and teleportation at useful fidelity?
papers.result: Yes. On ibm_phoenix, excluding bad components by re-purposing ancillas halves the distance-5 logical error per round from 1.9% to 0.9%, comparable to the best distance-3 patches. Lattice surgery between adjacent distance-3 codes gives logical Bell-state fidelity above 93%. Three logical qubits give state, Bell-pair and gate teleportation at 78–93%. A stability experiment with resets on every qubit every two rounds reaches about \(2\times10^{-7}\) failure probability at 170 rounds.
techniques: Bounding Bell-state fidelity from two stabilizer expectations
Ancilla re-purposing with gauge checks

papers.title: One-sided-DIQKD using any pure bipartite entangled state secure against all attacks
papers.authors: Bohnishikha Ghosh; Chithra Raj; Shubhayan Sarkar
papers.problem: In one-sided device-independent QKD, Bob’s measurements are trusted and Alice’s device is a black box, so security rests on quantum steering. Existing protocols use maximally entangled states, which are costly to make. Can every pure entangled state of any dimension yield a secret key in this setting, including with lossy detectors and noisy sources?
papers.result: Yes. In the noiseless case, self-testing of any pure state \(\sum_i\alpha_i|ii\rangle\) gives a key rate equal to its entanglement entropy. With depolarizing visibility \(\nu\) and efficiency \(\eta\) on Alice’s side, an entropic-uncertainty bound gives a closed-form rate that is affine in \(\eta\), and hence a critical efficiency for every pure state and visibility. The critical efficiency is 1/2 for maximally entangled states and rises only slowly as entanglement falls.
techniques: Key rate from the uncertainty relation with a trusted side
Critical efficiency from an affine rate, and a check on the printed formula

papers.title: Optimal probes for estimating the dephasing of a quantum spin system
papers.authors: Leonardo Ratini; Stefano Carretta; Francesco Albarelli
papers.problem: To estimate the strength of dephasing on a spin \(J\) (or \(2J\) qubits), which superposition of levels should be prepared? A spin cat state is optimal for weak Gaussian phase diffusion, but its coherence is the first to decay. Over what range does the cat stay optimal, and what works beyond it?
papers.result: For general dephasing channels, the QFI is concave in the probe populations and an ancilla never helps. The channel QFI is a second-order cone program whose dual variables are the optimal populations. For Gaussian diffusion the cat is globally optimal exactly for \(\Delta\le0.1424\) at \(J=1\) and \(\Delta\le0.065\) at \(J=3/2\); for larger \(J\) its range shrinks at least as \(1/J^2\). Beyond it, uniform superpositions, or a one-parameter interpolation between cat and uniform, are near optimal.
techniques: Concavity of the QFI in probe populations
Channel QFI as a cone program whose dual is the optimal probe

papers.title: Local Dephasing Sustains Continuous Time Crystals in a Spin-1/2 Ensemble
papers.problem: Pure dephasing destroys single-spin coherence and is normally counted as loss. In a fully connected ferromagnetic spin-\(1/2\) ensemble with local decay, can dephasing instead be what keeps a collective oscillation going, a continuous time crystal under time-independent dynamics?
papers.result: Yes. An exact operator identity shows that dephasing feeds energy into the transverse interaction, which local decay removes with a delay of order \(1/\Gamma_1\). In homogeneous mean field there is no periodic orbit without dephasing, and on a periodic orbit the delayed feedback exactly pays for the transverse damping. Liouvillian spectra for \(N=80\)–\(300\) show oscillatory decay rates falling as \(N^{-0.32}\) and \(N^{-0.46}\), with frequencies approaching the mean-field values.
techniques: Exact energy balance from an observable that commutes with the Hamiltonian
Cycle work of a lagged feedback variable

papers.title: Entanglement certification of attosecond light fields with photoelectron interferometry
papers.problem: High-harmonic generation is predicted to entangle the infrared driving field with extreme-ultraviolet harmonics. Standard optical certification needs local oscillators or photon-correlation detectors that barely exist at XUV frequencies. Can photoelectron interferometry (RABBIT), already routine in attosecond science, certify that entanglement on its own?
papers.result: Not from one sideband: every set of single-sideband moments has a fully separable explanation. Adding the two neighbouring sidebands supplies moments \(U\) and \(V\), and \(|Q|^2>UV\) then certifies IR–XUV entanglement through the partial transpose. A further bound \(|Q|>H(U,V)\) certifies genuine three-mode entanglement and is tight when \(U=0\). On model states, a displaced two-mode squeezed state is certified only in a window of displacement and squeezing, and a non-Gaussian GME family only for squeezing \(r<0.043\).
techniques: Partial-transpose moment matrices from the measured orderings
Biseparable bounds by isolating one Fock sector

papers.title: The Impact of Markovian Errors on Random Circuits
papers.authors: Anthony M. Polloreno; Timothy Proctor; Robin Blume-Kohout
papers.problem: Randomized benchmarking reports one error rate, but under gate-dependent noise it is unclear what that number measures. Average gate infidelity is gauge dependent, so it cannot be the answer. For small Markovian errors, how does each elementary error (Pauli-stochastic, over-rotation, axis tilt) enter the RB decay?
papers.result: For any gate set and sampling distribution forming a sequence-asymptotic unitary 2-design, Pauli-stochastic rates are the only errors that enter the decay linearly. Hamiltonian rates enter through a quadratic form that vanishes on gauge directions. For direct RB of \(\{X_{\pi/2},Y_{\pi/2}\}\) with probability \(p\) of \(X\), the form is explicit in two over-rotations and one relative axis tilt. Equal over-rotations \(\theta\) give \(r=3\theta^2/4\) at \(p=1/2\), three times each gate’s infidelity, and about 16.6 times at \(p=0.9\). For Clifford RB, a fixed form with weights \(1/9\) and \(1/18\) is filtered through the compilation.
techniques: First-order RB decay from a Choi-space projector
Gauge invariance forces the coherent term onto FOGI coordinates

papers.title: Problem-aware sampling for bias and variance reduction in randomised Hamiltonian simulation
papers.authors: Brian Coyle; Jonathan H. Fetherolf; Antonio Márquez Romero; Stefano Scali; Giuseppe Buonaiuto; Josh Kirsopp
papers.problem: qDRIFT approximates \(e^{-iHT}\) by random Pauli rotations sampled in proportion to \(|c_j|\), ignoring the initial state and the observable. Its estimators carry bias and variance that cost many steps and trajectories. When the goal is a single \(\langle O(T)\rangle\) from a known initial state, can the sampling distribution be tuned to the problem while keeping qDRIFT’s guarantees?
papers.result: Yes, with StateDRIFT. To fourth order in \(dt\), bias and variance depend on the distribution only through a few \(t=0\) quantities built from \(|\psi\rangle\), \(O\) and the Hamiltonian terms. This gives closed-form variance-optimal rules, an interpolating family that provably improves both bias and variance at one step for sign-definite inputs, and an optimized family for deeper circuits. For molecules of 6 to 18 qubits the dynamics resolves in 1.7–26 times fewer steps and 1.2–11 times fewer two-qubit gates; for BeH\(_2\) the gate count falls from 11,201 to 983. Mixing with 20% of the vanilla distribution bounds every reweighting by a factor of 5.
techniques: Neyman allocation for importance-sampled channels
Majorana degree counting fixes the RDM order

papers.title: FVQKD: A Formal Verification of Quantum Key Distribution Security in Rocq
papers.authors: Ruixuan Deng; Zhengfeng Ji; Jiayu Zhang; Li Zhou
papers.problem: QKD security rests on hand-checked proofs that chain smooth entropies, an entropic uncertainty relation, a sampling bound and the leftover hash lemma, drawn from several papers with differing conventions. Can the composable finite-key security of BB84 be machine-checked end to end, from a formal protocol program to the key-length theorem?
papers.result: Yes, in FVQKD, a Rocq development of about 151,000 lines, 102,000 of them new, with no admitted lemmas and only the kernel plus three standard axioms. It proves composable finite-key security of BB84 at the tight Tomamichel et al. bound, for every initial state and every adversary channel acting on a formally specified protocol program. Mechanization exposed a missing case in the published argument: after conditioning on the test passing, the smoothing parameter \(\varepsilon/\sqrt{p_{\rm pass}}\) can exceed 1, outside the domain of the uncertainty relation. A second proof branch using the abort probability repairs it, and the key-length formula is unchanged. A concrete instance with \(n=k=10^4\) certifies a 2000-bit key.
techniques: The finite-key bound as a chain of entropy inequalities
Split on the event probability when conditioning inflates a smoothing parameter

papers.title: Reset-Enhanced Dissipative Quantum Metrology
papers.authors: Silan Li; Qingjun Tong; Ruicheng Bao
papers.problem: Dissipation in open quantum sensors usually washes out parameter information. Can the simplest dissipative control, a channel that resets the probe to a fixed state at rate \(r\), increase the quantum Fisher information in steady-state and transient sensing without changing the Hamiltonian or adding a coherent drive?
papers.result: Sometimes, and the paper says exactly when. An exact identity for \(\partial_rF\) gives a first-order test for local enhancement. For a thermal qubit reset to its ground state, steady-state thermometry improves if and only if \(0<\beta\omega<\ln(2+\sqrt5)\) and \(r\) is below a threshold, with optimum \(r_{\rm opt}=\gamma(2+\sqrt5-e^{\beta\omega})/(e^{\beta\omega}-1)\). For diagonal dynamics, reset cannot change the leading short-time Fisher information of a static parameter, but it raises elapsed-time information immediately, roughly as \(r^2\). For frequency estimation with reset to \(|+\rangle\), the gain at \(t=1/\gamma\) is about 7 times, 91% of it from the coherence (eigenvector) part.
techniques: Response of the QFI to a control parameter through the SLD
Short-time expansion separating static parameters from time

papers.title: Photon localization: Local measurements, localized states, and causality
papers.problem: What does it mean for a photon to be localized in quantum field theory, where there is no position operator, the vacuum is entangled across regions, and no-go theorems (Hegerfeldt, Malament, Reeh–Schlieder) seem to forbid localized particles altogether?
papers.result: The review argues that localization should be defined through local measurement: a state is strictly localized to a spacetime region \(\mathcal O\) if no observable outside \(\mathcal O\) can tell it from the vacuum. With this definition, single photons (and any state with a bounded photon number) cannot be strictly localized, while coherent states, squeezed states and states arbitrarily close to single photons can. On-demand sources must produce strictly localized states.
techniques: Prove non-localizability from a nonvanishing vacuum matrix element
Build localized states from the polar part of a smeared field

papers.title: Discrete Time Liquids
papers.authors: Zuo Wang; Paul M. Schindler; Marin Bukov; Marios H. Michael
papers.problem: Time crystals break the discrete time-translation symmetry of a perfectly periodic drive. Can temporal order also emerge from noise, when the only drive is the thermal fluctuation of a cavity mode with finite coherence time?
papers.result: Yes. A two-dimensional classical spin lattice coupled to a thermal cavity mode locks to half the cavity frequency within a window of bath temperatures. When the cavity coherence time is short, single trajectories switch stochastically between the two period-doubled configurations. These switches, called time-solitons, destroy long-range temporal coherence while preserving local period doubling: a discrete time liquid. A one-parameter toy model with independent sign flips reproduces the full distribution of single-trajectory correlation times.
techniques: Treat a narrow-band thermal mode as a random-amplitude, random-phase drive
Separate defects from decay with three nested correlation times

papers.title: Normal-Form Characterization of Adaptivity and Entanglement in Pauli-Based Computation
papers.authors: Filipa C. R. Peres; Selman Ipek; Daniel Lovsted; Joshua Nevin; Anne Broadbent
papers.problem: Pauli-based computation (PBC) runs a Clifford+\(T\) circuit as a sequence of commuting Pauli measurements on magic states, chosen adaptively from earlier outcomes. The adaptive tree of measurements is exponentially large. Is there a compact description of how branches differ, comparable to flow in one-way computing?
papers.result: Yes. Every branch of the PBC tree is obtained from the all-zero reference branch by conjugating each observable with phase gates \(S\) on the magic qubits whose earlier outcomes were 1. This normal form groups measurements into adaptive layers, gives a duality with a computation-specific one-way computation, detects unnecessary magic qubits in polynomial rather than exponential time, and allows ahead-of-time compilation. The resulting circuits use on average about 50% fewer CNOTs and 40% less quantum memory than state-of-the-art compilers on random circuits.
techniques: Move outcome-dependent corrections onto the input state
Detect removable resources by checking one branch against a symmetry

papers.title: Transversal syndrome extraction: A unifying construction for measuring the error syndromes of any stabilizer code
papers.problem: Fault-tolerant syndrome extraction for a general stabilizer code is either deep (Shor’s method measures one stabilizer at a time with cat states) or wide (Steane’s method measures everything at once with a \(2n\)-qubit encoded ancilla). Configurable middle grounds were known only for CSS codes. Is there one for every stabilizer code?
papers.result: Yes. Partitioning the stabilizer generators into sets measured together, and building a matching ancilla stabilizer state from the generalized Steane ancilla, gives a family of transversal gadgets for any stabilizer code. Shor and Steane extraction appear as the two limits, so depth can be traded for width. For example, the full syndrome of an \([[8,2,3]]\) code can be measured with four layers of data–ancilla gates using at most 12 ancilla qubits. Simulated logical error rates fall between those of Shor and Steane extraction.
techniques: Design ancillas so that propagated stabilizers carry the syndrome and nothing else
Interpolate between two known gadgets by deleting rows and qubits

papers.title: Pure states are optimal for total energy-constrained quantum channel discrimination
papers.problem: When discriminating two bosonic channels with a probe of fixed mean photon number and no ancilla, is a pure probe always optimal? Convexity suggests yes, but the pure components of a mixed probe generally have different photon numbers, so the best component may break the energy budget.
papers.result: Yes. Every state of mean photon number \(\bar n\) is a mixture of pure states each with mean photon number exactly \(\bar n\), including for infinite rank. Combined with Lieb concavity, this shows that for any two channels some equal-energy pure probe does at least as well as any mixed probe. This holds for the quantum Chernoff exponent, for every Chernoff quantity \(Q_s\), and for the single-shot error probability.
techniques: Equalize a constraint across a decomposition by pairwise rotations
From concavity at one \(s\) to optimality of the minimized exponent

papers.title: Distributed dual-comb spectroscopy
papers.authors: Haowei Shi; Kartikeya Arora; Zheshen Zhang; Quntao Zhuang
papers.problem: Quantum-enhanced dual-comb spectroscopy uses squeezed or entangled frequency combs to beat shot noise over a broad band, and distributed quantum sensing uses entanglement across sites to estimate global quantities. Can one combine both, estimating weighted averages of absorption across many samples and many frequencies, with a single quantum light source?
papers.result: Yes. Each sample sits in a Mach–Zehnder interferometer with a bright classical comb in one port and a share of a single two-mode-squeezed comb, split \(K\) ways by a passive beam splitter, in the dark port. With splitter weights matched to the target weights, the variance of every weighted-average estimator falls by the squeezing gain \(G\). Splitters that do not depend on frequency force a trade-off between gases with different targets: for orthogonal targets the guaranteed advantage is \(2G/(G+1)\), at most 3 dB.
techniques: Match the entanglement splitter to the estimated linear functional
Bound multi-target advantage by a shared-resource geometry

papers.title: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
papers.authors: Jacques L. Pienaar; Eran Tal; Asya Ciftci
papers.problem: Quantum metrology speaks of estimating an unknown “true value”. Is that reading consistent when the estimated quantity is itself quantum and can become entangled with the probes?
papers.result: No, not without a cost. Embedding the parameter as an observable \(\hat\theta\) reproduces standard estimation whenever its state is diagonal. But five assumptions cannot all hold together: Uniqueness, Pre-existing Value and Independence (the realist reading of a true value), Entanglement between quantity and probes, and Completeness of the quantum state (no hidden variables). Dropping any one restores consistency.
techniques: Embed a classical parameter as a controlling quantum register
Locate a no-go theorem by listing jointly inconsistent assumptions

papers.title: Mixed State Deep Thermalization under Generic Quantum Errors
papers.problem: After chaotic dynamics, the states of a subsystem conditioned on measuring the rest follow a universal (Haar) distribution. What distribution emerges when local errors make those conditional states mixed?
papers.result: A universal one fixed by the error alone. The late-time ensemble of conditional states is the channel-induced ensemble, \(\tilde\rho=XMX^\dagger\) with \(X\) a complex Gaussian (Ginibre) matrix and Born weight \(\operatorname{Tr}XMX^\dagger\). Here \(M\) is the normalized Choi state of the error, and only its spectrum matters. This is derived for dual-unitary circuits, global Haar dynamics and local Haar circuits at large local dimension, and checked numerically in qubit circuits and kicked Ising dynamics.
techniques: A random-matrix reference ensemble built from the Choi state
Born-weighted moments of a projected ensemble

papers.title: The limits of magic-state distillation
papers.problem: How few noisy T states can any stabilizer protocol, however adaptive, postselected or multistage, consume to output a magic state with error \(O(p^d)\)?
papers.result: Exact minima for small factories. Fault tolerance of any protocol reduces to projection onto a single stabilizer code, and for rational targets a fault pattern is harmful exactly when its complement is. Exhaustive search then shows: quadratic distillation of one T state needs exactly 9 inputs (a new 9-input factory is found), controlled-S needs 8, and the 8-input CCZ factory is optimal. At every order \(d\), one T state needs at least \(2d\) inputs.
techniques: Reduce all protocols to one code projection
Galois conjugation pairs complementary faults

papers.title: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
papers.authors: Hongrui Chen; Zhiyan Ding; Jianfeng Lu
papers.problem: Does relative entropy decay at a rate independent of system size under quasi-local quantum Gibbs samplers for non-commuting Hamiltonians?
papers.result: Yes, in two regimes. For the Gaussian KMS Gibbs sampler, both the \(L^2\) logarithmic Sobolev inequality and the modified one (MLSI) hold with system-size-independent constants: in one dimension at every finite temperature, and in any fixed dimension at sufficiently high temperature. This gives \(O(\log n+\log(1/\epsilon))\) mixing time.
techniques: Transport a functional inequality along a unitary path
Upgrade Rényi-2 contraction to relative-entropy contraction with tensor powers

papers.title: One-shot entanglement generation and distillation via Petz recovery and binary hypothesis testing
papers.problem: How much entanglement can two laboratories obtain from one use of a noisy channel or one copy of a shared noisy state, and can the answer be expressed as a binary hypothesis-testing cost?
papers.result: An \((m,\varepsilon)\) entanglement generation or one-way distillation protocol exists whenever \(e_{d,m}(1-e_{d,m}/dm)\le\varepsilon\). Here \(e_{d,m}\) is the optimal error for testing \(\rho_{AB}\) against an explicit alternative \(B_{d,m}\propto dI_A\otimes\rho_B-\rho_{AB}\). Consequently \(\log_2m\le I_H^{\varepsilon-\nu}(A\rangle B)-\log_2(1/\nu)\) suffices, and repeated use gives \(nI_c+\sqrt{nV_c}\,\Phi^{-1}(\varepsilon)-\tfrac12\log_2n-c\) ebits.
techniques: Apply Cheng’s trace inequality before averaging over random codes
From a binary test to an integer code dimension

papers.title: A simple proof of unitary parallelization via port-based teleportation
papers.problem: Can port-based teleportation be implemented by an elementary low-depth circuit, and does that give a simple proof that every unitary can be parallelized?
papers.result: Yes. A single reflection on Alice’s registers implements port-based teleportation with \(N\) ports and dimension \(d\) to diamond error \(2(d^2-1)/N+\delta\), in depth \(\operatorname{polylog}(Nd/\delta)\). Feeding Choi states of \(U\) into the ports implements any \(n\)-qubit unitary in depth \(\operatorname{poly}(n,\log1/\varepsilon)\) and width \(2^{O(n)}\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon)\).
techniques: Teleport with a single reflection
Read out sums of swaps with parallel random SWAP tests

papers.title: Conservation in Every Quantum Measurement Outcome?
papers.authors: E. Okon; D. Sudarsky; M. Wiedemann
papers.problem: Does including the system that prepared a superposition restore a conservation law in every individual measurement outcome, as Collins and Popescu have proposed?
papers.result: The authors argue that it does not, in the sense claimed. The need for a physical preparer is postulated rather than derived from the relativity of angle. The preparer never holds a definite value, so what the mechanism restores is a shifted probability distribution. A preparation that conserves one observable can disturb a noncommuting one. For energy, the preparation interaction breaks the additivity the bookkeeping relies on.
techniques: Test a conservation mechanism against the whole symmetry group
Overlap factors set how broad a hidden partner must be

papers.title: An entanglement band structure for general multiqubit states
papers.problem: Majorana pictured a symmetric multiqubit state as points on the sphere. Can a comparable geometric picture be given for general states, whose entanglement classes form continuous families?
papers.result: Projecting one qubit onto a direction \(\mathbf n\) leaves a conditional state of the others. Its entanglement invariants are the eigenvalues, called bands, of a non-Hermitian matrix \(L(u)\). For five qubits there are four bands, which meet at 24 exceptional points where the conditional state changes entanglement family. Together they form one Riemann surface of genus nine, which fixes the five-qubit entanglement class up to finitely many choices.
techniques: Read SLOCC invariants from a holomorphic matrix pencil
Count exceptional points and the genus from the discriminant

papers.title: Injection is all you need: parallel universal logic in high-rate concatenated self-dual codes
papers.authors: Joseph Sullivan; David Amaro; Michael A. Perlin
papers.problem: High-rate codes store many logical qubits per block but make it hard to act on a chosen subset. How can they run parallel, addressable, universal logic?
papers.result: In concatenated self-dual codes with transversal global \(H\) and \(S\), any logical Clifford is injected by consuming at most 9 CSS resource states. \(T\) gates on any subset need one \(\ket H^{\otimes K}\) magic state and one CSS state, so a circuit of \(T\)-depth \(D_T\) needs at most \(12D_T\) resource states. A Hadamard parity check repeated at each concatenation level gives magic states whose undetected error is \(O(p^{2^L})\). In simulations at \(p=5\times10^{-4}\), this concatenated cultivation needed about ten times less spacetime than surface-code cultivation for the two distance-4 codes.
techniques: Reduce every Clifford layer to CSS resource states
Hadamard-parity flags, and why one parity stalls at second order

papers.title: Finite Classification of Transversal Diagonal Gates Beyond Stabilizer Codes
papers.authors: Xi He; Chao Zhang; Shilin Huang; Bei Zeng
papers.problem: Code-preserving diagonal phases of general (nonadditive) qubit codes can vary continuously. Can the transversal diagonal gates of such codes still be classified exhaustively?
papers.result: Yes, at fixed code parameters. For a code of distance at least two, every projective logical action of a transversal diagonal gate has a physical representative of finite order \(q\), with \(m\mid q\) and \(q\) bounded in terms of \(n\) and \(K\) alone; \(q\le9\) for six qubits at distance three. For exact ((6,2,3)) codes, 66 candidate symmetry classes reduce to 15 realizable ones, with diagonal logical groups \(C_2\), \(C_3\) or \(C_5\). The order-five code is unique up to local unitaries and qubit permutations. It is also the shortest distance-3 qubit code whose transversal logical group cannot be conjugated into the Clifford group.
techniques: Strip continuous phases that act only as logical scalars
Subset-sum sectors and moment matching as a staged filter

papers.title: Tight Bounds on the Randomized Communication Complexity of Vector-in-Subspace
papers.problem: One quantum message of \(\lceil\log_2n\rceil\) qubits solves Vector-in-Subspace exactly. How many bits does an interactive classical protocol need?
papers.result: \(\Theta(\sqrt n)\) bits. A lower bound of \(\Omega(\sqrt n)\) holds for bounded-error randomized protocols with any number of rounds, matching Raz’s \(O(\sqrt n)\) protocol. It improves the \(\Omega(n^{1/3})\) bound of Klartag and Regev and removes the total-rank restriction in Grupel’s \(\Omega(\sqrt n)\) result.
techniques: Complex Gaussian lifts perform the Wick corrections
A vanishing even moment bounds a real center

papers.title: Quantum f-divergences from retrodiction: a unifying classical variational principle
papers.problem: A classical \(f\)-divergence has several inequivalent quantum extensions. Can they all be obtained from one operational optimization?
papers.result: Yes. Compare a forward prepare-and-measure process with its reverse, obtained by Petz retrodiction relative to a reference prior \(\gamma\), subject to prescribed averages \(\rho\) and \(\sigma\). The minimum classical \(f\)-divergence between their complete records is attained by one spectral implementation, simultaneously for every operator-convex \(f\). A flat prior gives the standard (Petz) divergence, Umegaki for relative entropy. A prior equal to \(\rho\) or \(\sigma\) gives the maximal divergence, Belavkin–Staszewski for relative entropy, and power priors \(\gamma\propto\sigma^t\) give the geodesic family between them.
techniques: Two operator-Jensen steps remove the implementation freedom
The retrodiction prior selects the quantum divergence

papers.title: Dimension-free marginal inequalities for pure three-party states
papers.problem: Which spectra can the three one-party marginals of a pure three-party state have, with inequalities that hold in every local dimension?
papers.result: A lifting theorem produces new valid inequalities from old ones by peeling off one party’s largest Schmidt component and applying Horn’s inequalities to the other two. Starting from Klyachko’s first-row bound, at most two lifting steps reproduce every facet of the marginal polytope for local dimension up to 4, and 455 of the 466 facet classes for dimension 5.
techniques: Peel off the largest Schmidt component
Combine Horn triples with Abel summation

papers.title: Trapped-ion-based quantum repeater node across a 17 km metropolitan fiber
papers.authors: K. Fabitha; T. Runggaldier; A. Winkler; F. Bernecker; J. Bate; M. Canteri; J. Helgert; T. E. Northup; V. Krutyanskiy; B. P. Lanyon
papers.problem: Can a trapped-ion repeater node distribute entanglement over deployed city fiber rather than a laboratory spool?
papers.result: A two-ion node in Innsbruck entangled a photon sent through 17 km of rented municipal fiber with a photon detected locally. The Bell-state fidelity was \(81.6^{+1.9}_{-1.4}\%\) (with feed-forward simulated), at 0.69 successes per second. Storing the first ion qubit raised the success probability 13.6-fold over sending both photons without memory.
techniques: Store the qubit for the fast link, not the slow one
Correct a drifting fiber by tomography and inversion

papers.title: The Four-Qubit Hyperbolic Quadric Has Contextuality Degree 315
papers.authors: Zhengyu Li; Amandeep Gupta; Vijay Ganesh
papers.problem: How many of the 1575 three-observable constraints on a four-qubit hyperbolic quadric must every noncontextual value assignment break?
papers.result: Exactly 315, proving a conjecture based on heuristic searches. In every optimal assignment each of the 40,320 doilies has exactly three violated lines, and the 240 possible violated sets are all copies of the dual polar space DW(5,2).
techniques: Read a lower bound from parity alone
Average over a symmetric cover, rounding locally

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Classical Simulation of BosonSampling under Any Constant-Fraction Photon Loss
papers.problem: Does lossy BosonSampling remain hard to simulate classically when a fixed fraction of the photons survives?
papers.result: Not under the conditions studied. For every fixed survival fraction \(n/N\in(0,1)\), Haar-random interferometers and \(M=\Omega(n^2N)\) modes, a classical algorithm samples within total variation distance \(\varepsilon\) of the collision-collapsed output distribution, for a \(1-\delta\) fraction of interferometers, in time \(\mathrm{poly}(M,N,\varepsilon^{-1},\delta^{-1})\). The same holds for every fixed transmission probability \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
techniques: Decompose an average over random survivors
Sum over subsets with color coding

papers.title: Correlated decoding loses the surface code’s effective distance below threshold
papers.authors: César Hernando de la Fuente; Joonas Majaniemi; Evert van Nieuwenburg; Felix Frohnert
papers.problem: Does two-pass correlated decoding of the surface code keep its advantage far below threshold?
papers.result: Not with the standard reweighting rule. Under circuit-level noise some size-\((d-1)/2\) fault configurations cause logical failures, so the logical error rate scales like \(p^{(d-1)/2}\) instead of \(p^{(d+1)/2}\). At \(d=3\) and \(p=10^{-5}\), correlated matching fails about 4.4 times as often as plain matching. Scaling the conditional edge probabilities by an error-rate-dependent factor \(\alpha^*(p)\) restores the distance scaling and a steady advantage.
techniques: Count the independent faults behind a correction
Regularize the update with one error-rate-dependent parameter

papers.title: Randomness Certification from Statistically Hiding Commitments
papers.problem: What cryptographic assumption lets a classical verifier certify randomness from a single untrusted quantum device, secure against quantum side information?
papers.result: A statistically hiding bit commitment that is computationally binding against quantum senders suffices; stronger notions such as collapse-binding are not needed. Consequently, post-quantum one-way permutations suffice. Trapdoor claw-free functions give an efficient verifier, and the quantum random-oracle model gives certification with no further assumption but an inefficient verifier.
techniques: Hide a BB84 basis inside two commitment openings
Turn a predictor into two openings

papers.title: Pump-Free Microwave-Optical Bell Pair Generation for Teleportation-Based Quantum Transduction
papers.problem: How can superconducting processors connect to optical networks while avoiding complications from optical pumping?
papers.result: Spin-mediated sources are predicted to herald microwave–optical Bell pairs at roughly 1–28 kHz, with fidelities of 0.86–0.99 depending on the platform. The pairs are intended for teleportation-based transduction.
techniques: Separate resource generation from state transfer
Use an intermediate spin as an interface

papers.title: Information Causality Characterizes the Set of Quantum Correlations in the Simplest Bell Scenario
papers.problem: Can an information principle recover the quantum boundary in the simplest Bell experiment?
papers.result: Generalized information causality implies the Tsirelson–Landau–Masanes criterion on the four renormalized correlators, so it recovers the quantum boundary of that correlator projection. A separate example shows that it also excludes some correlations that macroscopic locality allows.
techniques: Keep the full measurement record
Expand around zero capacity

papers.title: Spurious quantum correlations
papers.authors: Shashaank Khanna; Matthew F. Pusey; Roger Colbeck
papers.problem: Can correlations that appear nonclassical acquire a classical explanation when the assumed causal structure changes?
papers.result: The authors identify correlations with classical explanations in alternative causal structures without fine tuning, and other correlations that resist such explanations.
techniques: Search over causal explanations
Separate statistical fit from physical admissibility

papers.title: Quantum error correction at ultra-low overhead
papers.authors: Zhide Lu; Weikang Li; Dong-Ling Deng
papers.problem: Can quantum error-correcting codes combine high encoding rates, tolerable noise, and feasible neutral-atom operations?
papers.result: Cornucopia codes reach encoding rates just above 1/2 at distances 6 to 18 and pseudo-thresholds above 0.4% under circuit-level noise. Their 12-layer syndrome cycle is carried out by rigid moves of whole atom blocks.
techniques: Design the code and its circuit together
Certify distance and count resources consistently

papers.title: A solution to 2-copy distillability of Werner states
papers.authors: Jinshi Fu; Li Gao; Sang-Jun Park
papers.problem: Can two copies of a Werner state yield distillable entanglement when one copy cannot?
papers.result: For every local dimension \(d\), a Werner state \(\rho_\alpha\) is two-copy distillable exactly when it is one-copy distillable (\(\alpha<-\tfrac12\)). States with \(-\tfrac12\le\alpha<-\tfrac1d\) are therefore NPT but not two-copy distillable.
techniques: Turn distillation into an operator test
Use symmetry to isolate a boundary case

papers.title: Quantum error correction with the toric code
papers.problem: Can neutral-atom logical memories sustain repeated error correction while replacing lost atoms?
papers.result: Twisted toric-code memories on 32 and 64 atoms (\([[16,1,(4,3)]]\) and \([[32,1,(6,4)]]\)) run for up to 90 and 70 syndrome cycles with atom reloading. Over four to eight cycles, the larger code has the lower logical error.
techniques: Rotate data and ancilla roles
Make replenishment part of the computation
